final_message:
I fixed it, and all 18 tests now pass (8 were failing before). There were two bugs in `fiscal/calendar.py`.

| Bug | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `_nearest_saturday` only ever went back to the previous Saturday | Year ends never landed in February. For example, FY2024 ended Jan 25, 2025 instead of Feb 1, 2025, so early-February days were put in the wrong fiscal year. | It now picks whichever Saturday is within 3 days, before or after: `d + timedelta(days=(5 - d.weekday() + 3) % 7 - 3)` |
| `_period_lengths` added the 53rd week to `lengths[0]` | In 53-week years the extra week went into period 1 instead of period 12, as SPEC §4 requires. | It now adds it to `lengths[-1]` |

**Check:**
```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
Ran 18 tests in 0.002s
OK
```
I also listed which years from 2015 to 2029 come out as 53-week years: FY2017, FY2023 and FY2028, each ending Feb 3. That's the expected roughly 5–6 year cycle, and FY2017 matches the published NRF calendar.

**State:** only `fiscal/calendar.py` changed (`git status --short` → ` M fiscal/calendar.py`). I haven't committed anything; tell me if you want a commit.

Any merch reports generated with the old code are wrong in two ways. Years that should end in early February had their year-end and period dates assigned to the wrong fiscal year. And in 53-week years, periods 1–12 were all off by a week. Those reports should be re-run.
